name: v2.4.1.100_canary_2026-10-31
body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Timeouts with remote sources and slow destinations

When a backup reads from a remote source, such as an SMB share or a cloud drive, that is faster than the destination, the reads are paused while a volume is uploaded. The timeout kept counting during these pauses and could fail the transfer although the remote service was responding. The timeout for almost all backends now only counts the time spent waiting for the remote service, not the time Duplicati itself is busy. The SMB backend got the same treatment directly, as it controls the flow itself.

A related problem made SMB and some other backends report incomplete data as a successful backup: when a stalled read hit the inactivity timeout, the timeout handler closed the stream, which took the error away. The error is now kept. SMB delete and rename also failed silently on an unexpected return code, which is now reported.

More timeout fixes:

- The Azure Blob backend set up its timeout stream but did not use it, so timeouts were ignored.
- The SMB client used the library default of 5 seconds when writing chunks to the destination. It now uses `--read-write-timeout`, which defaults to 30 seconds.
- `--list-timeout` was not applied to SFTP and MinIO listings, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Storj transfers that stopped moving were waited for forever. They now fail when no bytes have moved for `--read-write-timeout`, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A timeout in a synchronous operation did not return when the task was cancelled, which could leave tasks stuck.
- A cancellation by the caller was reported as a timeout, and a timeout could escape as a cancellation, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Resuming remote source reads

A file read from a remote source is now wrapped in a resuming stream. If the connection is lost while reading, the stream reconnects and continues from where it stopped. The data up to that point is read again and hashed, to make sure the file did not change in the meantime. A backend interface for resuming with a range request was added, so backends that support it can resume without re-reading, but no backend implements it yet.

A remote source that dropped or truncated a file used to have the partial file stored as if it was complete. Truncated files are now rejected with a warning and not stored.

# Source folders that cannot be read

A source folder that exists but cannot be listed, for example on a failed drive, only gave a warning. The backup then stored a version without any of its files, and the retention policy could remove the versions that still had them. The backup is now stopped, as for a missing source, unless `--allow-missing-source` is set, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

A backup that was stopped before it started processing files uploaded an empty version as the latest, and warned that the source was likely misconfigured. No version is created now, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Placeholder files from a sync tool, such as OneDrive, Dropbox or Google Drive, and files moved to offline storage fail to read with a generic error. These errors are now recognized and reported with a message that points to `--exclude-non-local-files`.

# Dry run no longer changes the database

A backup with `--dry-run` did not touch the remote data, but the compact step committed its decision to the local database. On the next real run, the recorded decision was carried out and files were deleted. The dry run no longer updates the database.

# Database downgrade scripts stored in the database

Until now, downgrading a local database required the downgrade script shipped with the newer version, so the downgrade had to be done before uninstalling it. The upgrade and downgrade scripts are now stored in the databases themselves, in a new `SchemaScript` table. From this release on, the bundled `duplicati-database-tool` can downgrade a database written by a newer version by using the scripts stored in the database, even if the tool does not know that schema. Downgrades are still started manually. The schema version is not changed by this release.

The default for `duplicati-database-tool downgrade` is now the newest version the tool itself supports, so a downgrade from the next version needs no explicit version. Downgrading over several versions requires the target version to be given. The tool also no longer mistakes a local database with an index or view named `Schedule` for a server database, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Restore fixes

- A block that could not be read from its volume stopped the whole restore. Only the files that use the block are now reported as failed, and the other files are restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562. When the database places a block in a volume that does not hold it, the error now names the block instead of failing with a null reference.
- A restore that could not restore some files exited with code 0. It now exits with code 3, as a backup that finished with errors does, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- When a priority file, such as the disk layout of a disk image, fails, the error now says that the restore was stopped because of it and names the file, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- With `--restore-symlink-metadata`, the extended attributes and the read-only attribute of a symbolic link were applied to the file it points to, also when that file is outside the restore folder. The extended attributes are now set on the link itself, and the attributes are skipped for links, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- On Linux, restoring the creation time overwrote the last write time that had just been restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The legacy restore engine did not count restored symbolic links, so restoring only a link ended with a warning that nothing was restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Repair and dlist files

Three problems with the names and times of dlist files were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- A dlist upload that fails is retried under a name one second later. Backups, synthetic filelists and purges did not record the fileset time in the file, so after a recreate such a version was one second late. The time is now recorded in every dlist file.
- A retried dlist upload after a repair or purge left a placeholder version dated 1970-01-01 in the version list until the next backup, and restoring that version failed.
- Repairing a missing dlist file gave the replacement a name at least one second after the original, which could put it after a newer version. The file is now uploaded again under its own name, and the search for a free name stops after the configured number of tries.

# Recovery tool

The recovery tool can now add encryption to a backup that was made without encryption, with the new `--add-encryption` option.

Recompressing to the same format uploaded the new file over the original name, and the following delete removed it, emptying the destination. Files that keep their name are now left in place, and `--reencrypt` warns when the files are not encrypted, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Reporting

Thanks @JamBalaya56562 for a series of fixes to the report modules:

- Values put into report templates were used as a regex replacement string, so a file name or option value containing `$` sequences corrupted the report body. The keys were also expanded in several passes over the already inserted values, so text such as `%backup-name%` inside a log line was expanded too, and a key with regex characters stopped the report. Values are now inserted literally and keys are expanded once.
- A failing HTTP report, status report or XMPP target skipped the remaining targets. Each target is now tried on its own.
- A report that failed to send made the operation a warning, but the job log did not show why. The stored result now includes the warnings and errors logged after it was written.
- A failing `--run-script-before` script or an option that failed validation stopped the operation before the report modules were set up, so no report was sent.
- The command line printed "Backup completed successfully!" also when a script stopped the backup or it ended with errors.
- A compact that changed something was logged twice in the job log, and the database was vacuumed twice.

The `Reason` field of restore test reports is now passed on in reduced reporting mode.

# Storage providers

- Google Workspace files were read fully into memory before being backed up, which used a lot of memory and failed for files above 2 GB. The data is now streamed in chunks, and the same approach is applied to Microsoft 365. The Google Workspace module also follows the standard timeout options, and chat attachments are stored with their content instead of their metadata.
- The progress bar during a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace delta walk often jumped from 0 to 100%. The walk now reports its progress as it goes.
- Google answers both a missing permission and a rate limit with 403, and the error body that tells them apart was dropped. Google Drive and Google Cloud Storage now report Google's reason, and rate limits are retried with backoff, also for the chunks of a resumable upload, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A Google Drive upload that timed out on the client could still be completed by Drive, leaving a second copy that a delete did not remove. All copies of the name are now deleted, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The B2 retry logic now follows the B2 guidelines, and a bug that could truncate listings was fixed.
- SMB left file handles open on the server when a get, delete or rename failed, and a failed close replaced the listing error with "Not enough credits", thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The SharePoint v2 backend required `--site-id` and never looked the site up from the URL. The site is now found from the URL, and a `--site-id` that names another site is reported as a conflict, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Server and user interface

- A system status endpoint was added as a websocket subscription. It reports CPU and memory usage, the transfer rates of the backends and the paths currently being read. The new UI uses it for its status page.
- The restore test API from the previous canary is now a v2 API and is reported as an API extension.
- Behind a reverse proxy that sets `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, the refresh cookie is now set on the prefixed path, so logins are persisted.
- The login and signin pages no longer bundle jQuery 2.0.3, which has known XSS issues, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- `--dblock-size`, `--prefix`, `--compression-module` and `--encryption-module` can be changed on an existing backup again. The previous canary stored them in the database and refused the change.
- Operations other than backup warned that `--store-task-config` is not supported.
- Two connection tests of the same destination at once, which the UI does when Continue is pressed while the folder-creating test is still running, interfered with each other's test file. Each test now uses its own file name, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Deleting a sync job with "delete remote files" failed and left the job in place. The option is ignored for sync jobs and the synced copy is kept. Restore and the other backup operations are refused on a sync job with a message, instead of failing with a database upgrade error, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The old UI showed the raw `%home%` path instead of "Home" in the source list when the system information arrived late, and the add backup page failed when the backup defaults loaded late, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- `--webservice-webroot` was ignored in release builds and in debug builds, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- macOS sleep prevention now uses power assertions instead of running `caffeinate`, so the kernel clears them when the process exits.
- Isolated runners now communicate over a named pipe instead of stdin and stdout, so output from the process cannot interfere, and tracing of this communication can be enabled.

# Other fixes

- Slow query monitoring counted the time callers spent between rows, so a query could be reported as running for an hour during the consistency check, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A backup's notifications are dismissed with one database update after a run, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The tray icon's request queue was shared between connections in the same process, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- HTTP clients were created from a stopped server's disposed factory, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A leftover debug line was printed to stderr on Linux when a timestamp was set on a filesystem with coarser precision, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The AutoTune tool shipped as `Duplicati.CommandLine.AutoTuneTool` without a `duplicati-autotune-tool` link on Linux and macOS, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The acknowledgements were updated.

## Detailed list of changes

name: v2.4.1.0_stable_2026-10-29
body:
# About this release

This release builds on version 2.4.0.1 with a large number of bug fixes, and adds three new features: incremental (delta) backups of Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, and restore tests that can run after backups and be switched on remotely from the console.

The local database format is updated by this release. See "Downgrading" below before going back to an earlier version.

## Delta walk for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace

Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace backups no longer need to list every item on every run. The providers now store a delta token with each backup and use the Microsoft Graph and Google change APIs, so later backups list only what was created, changed, moved or removed since the previous backup and carry the rest forward from it.

For Microsoft 365 this covers mail folders, SharePoint and group document libraries. For Google Workspace it covers Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Contacts. Delta tracking is enabled by default. The first backup, the first backup after the local database is recreated, and the backup after one that was stopped still list everything in full.

Delta tracking can be turned off per service with `--office365-disable-mail-delta`, `--office365-disable-drive-delta`, `--google-disable-gmail-delta`, `--google-disable-drive-delta`, `--google-disable-calendar-delta` and `--google-disable-contacts-delta`. If a document library reports more changes than `--office365-drive-delta-max-items` or `--google-drive-delta-max-items`, the library is listed in full instead.

A backup that combines a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace source with the USN change journal or `--changed-files` is now refused with an error, as the two mechanisms cannot be combined.

## Restore tests

A new restore test operation restores a sample of a backup from the remote destination into a temporary folder and verifies it, so the backup is regularly proven to be restorable. It is available as the `restore-test` command in the command line and in ServerUtil, and through the server API.

The sample is chosen with `--restore-test-mode`: a number of random files, a percentage of the backup size, every file, or a rolling mode that prefers files that have not been verified recently. The test can be limited with `--restore-test-max-download-size` and `--restore-test-max-runtime`, can rebuild a temporary database from the destination with `--restore-test-recreate-database`, and can compare the restored files with the source files with `--restore-test-compare-source`.

Set `--perform-restore-test-after` to run a restore test as the last step of a backup whenever the previous test is older than the given interval. When the machine is connected to the Duplicati console, the console can set this interval for its backups, so restore tests can be switched on remotely. A restore test after a backup does not change the result of the backup, but a failed test is reported with its own notification.

## Improved support for Sync jobs

With this version, Sync jobs now store their logs so the logs can be viewed after the job has completed. Several places where the Sync job was showing options that were only relevant to restores are now updated.

## Other new features

- Backup versions can be given a label with the `set-version-label` command. The labels are also stored on the destination, so a database recreate keeps them.
- Point-in-time access to a destination: with `--remote-point-in-time`, the S3 and Duplicati Storage destinations read the destination as it was at the given time, using bucket versioning. The destination is read-only in this mode.
- Report modules can send reports for other operations than backups, chosen with `--send-http-operations`, `--send-mail-operations`, `--send-xmpp-operations` and `--send-telegram-operations`. Backup reports remain the default.
- A restore on an existing backup can now carry additional advanced options.
- The new `--disable-secret-provider` option disables the default secret provider, the configured secret provider, or both. `--disable-default-secret-provider` still works but is deprecated. The server now also reports which secret provider is active.
- Duplicati Storage can be used as a secondary target, and supports object locking.
- Uploads to Google Cloud Storage now carry a CRC32 checksum.
- SMB servers that require SMB 3.1.1 can be used with `--enable-smb311`.
- Neon Object Storage has been added to the list of S3 providers.

## Changed behavior

- A backup that asks for object locks on a bucket or container that does not have locking enabled now completes with a warning that no locks were applied, instead of failing. This applies to S3, B2, Azure, Google Cloud Storage and Duplicati Storage.
- Options in source and destination urls are now validated, so an option that no module supports is reported with a warning.
- The Microsoft 365 site classifications "Classic" and "Communication" have been removed, as they never matched any site.
- When a restore does not specify overwrite, restore permissions or skip metadata, the settings of the backup and the server defaults now apply instead of turning them off.

## Downgrading

This release updates the local database from version 19 to version 22 and the sync database to version 1. Version 2.4.0.1 cannot open the newer databases. To go back to 2.4.0.1, downgrade the databases with the DatabaseTool `downgrade` command first. Its default target versions now match 2.4.0.1, so no version options are needed.

## Fixes

Aborting a backup no longer waits for a stuck source listing, file open, size or metadata read, and a stop or abort that arrives before the operation is ready is kept.

Restores keep an appended file when restoring without `--overwrite`, do not read through a link when restoring a symbolic link to a file, keep the drive letter folder when restoring Windows paths in place, and stop when `--restore-path` has no value. A partial restore no longer warns about the folders it has to create. Repair keeps the time and order of the versions when it replaces missing dlist files, and a later database recreate keeps them too.

On Windows, a local folder destination whose url contains `@` or carries options in its query string is now read correctly, and symbolic links created by WSL are backed up as links. Backups leave the write-ahead log files of their own database out.

The server and tray icon have fixes to notifications, task state, pause and resume events, preload settings, update checks, the login token cookie behind a reverse proxy, and the Agent. Control file restores are protected against path traversal, and the recovery tool and the Agent pre-shared key have been hardened.

Backend fixes include Jottacloud timeouts and parallel downloads, Storj uploads, WebDAV listings on Windows and Linux, the S3 list API version option, HashiCorp Vault JSON secrets, GnuPG on slow systems, and the User-Agent header sent by WebDAV, pCloud and the updater.

SQLite has been updated to 3.54.0, built for older Linux distributions, and StreamJsonRpc and MimeKit have been updated for security advisories.

## Detailed list of changes:

name: v2.4.0.105_canary_2026-10-24
body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Point-in-time restores from versioned storage

Storage that supports versioning keeps a new version of a file each time it is overwritten or deleted. The new `--remote-point-in-time` option makes Duplicati read the storage as it was at a given time, either relative such as `--remote-point-in-time=2D4h` or as an absolute time. While the option is set, the destination is read-only, and listing and downloading use the latest version available at that time.

This makes it possible to restore from a damaged or tampered versioned destination without first moving the old versions into a new bucket by hand.

Object lock handling was also improved. A destination that does not support object locks is now detected, so Duplicati no longer retries the lock for every file, and a lock failure caused by missing support is reported as a warning since the backup or repair itself completed.

# Duplicati Storage improvements

Duplicati Storage now supports object locks, and it can be used as a secondary destination in a multi-destination backup.

# Delta tracking for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace

Backups of Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace now store the delta tokens returned by the services. Each following backup starts from the stored tokens and only lists the items that changed, instead of walking the full mailbox or drive. This can make repeated backups of large tenants much faster and reduces throttling, at the cost of some memory and a larger local database. The progress counter is not shown while a delta walk runs, as the total is not known.

Delta tracking is on by default and can be turned off per item type:

- Microsoft 365: `--office365-disable-mail-delta` and `--office365-disable-drive-delta`
- Google Workspace: `--google-disable-gmail-delta`, `--google-disable-drive-delta`, `--google-disable-calendar-delta` and `--google-disable-contacts-delta`

If a drive reports more changes than `--office365-drive-delta-max-items` or `--google-drive-delta-max-items` (default 100000), the drive is walked in full instead.

Google Workspace now also treats a 403 caused by an exceeded quota, and similar quota messages, as a temporary failure and retries with backoff.

# Local database update

The delta tokens are stored in the local backup database, which requires an update of the local database schema to version 22. The update adds a table for source provider state and is applied to all backup databases on first use, not only those for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. After the update, the local databases can no longer be opened by earlier versions of Duplicati.

If you need to downgrade, the bundled database tool (`duplicati-database-tool`) can downgrade the local databases back to version 21. Downgrading removes the stored delta tokens, so the next backup of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace walks all items again, but otherwise causes no data loss.

# Restore tests from the console

The console can now start restore tests on a connected machine, either on a schedule or on demand. The `duplicati-server-util` tool also has a new `restore-test` command.

# Secret provider switches

The secret provider in use, and the default secret provider, are now reported in the system information. New options make it possible to disable the configured secret provider, the default secret provider, or both.

# No more 32-bit Windows builds

The 32-bit Windows (x86) packages are no longer part of the regular releases. They can still be built from source.

# SQLite update

SQLite is updated to 3.54.0. The custom build for ARMv7 has been removed, and the Linux requirement is once again GLIBC 2.28.

# Files missing from backups

Three cases where files were left out of a backup without a warning were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- When one source is inside another, the inner source was dropped if a folder on the way held an ignore marker such as `CACHEDIR.TAG`, had excluded attributes, was marked as excluded by an extended attribute, or was a symbolic link that is not followed. The files below the inner source were then missing from the backup.
- With `--usn-policy`, a source that is a single file was checked against the folders above it up to the drive root. As the root is usually hidden and a system folder, the file was excluded from the second backup on when hidden or system files were excluded.
- A WebDAV share mapped to a drive letter on Windows could not be used as a source, as the listing returned names with a trailing null character. The file picker failed, and a backup never finished.

Symbolic links made by WSL are also read as symbolic links on Windows, instead of failing with a warning on every run.

# Symbolic links and permissions

With `--symlink-policy=follow`, the owner, permissions and extended attributes of a linked file were taken from the link, so with `--restore-permissions` a file came back with mode 0777 and its extended attributes were lost. These are now read from the target.

With `--restore-symlink-metadata` and `--restore-permissions`, restoring a symbolic link set the permissions on the file the link points to, making it world-writable. The permissions are now only set on entries that are not links.

Thanks @JamBalaya56562 for both fixes.

# Restore fixes

More restore problems were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- Restoring without `--overwrite` cut a file that had data appended since the backup back to the backed-up length, losing the appended data. The file is now kept, and the backed-up version is restored beside it.
- Restoring a symbolic link to a file failed with errors when the target was missing, or when a link that points nowhere was already at the path.
- Relative symbolic link targets now have their separators mapped when restoring on another operating system.
- A Windows backup restored to the original location on Linux or macOS was put in a folder named `C:` in the working folder. It is now restored below `/C/` as intended.
- `--restore-path` written without `=`, such as `--restore-path D:\target`, made the restore go to the original location. It now stops with an error.
- An empty file that cannot be created is now reported as not restored.
- A legacy dry run restore no longer reports errors for files it did not write, and reports the number of files it would restore.
- Unchecking a root folder in the old UI restore picker could leave files below it selected, and restored.

# DatabaseTool cleanup

`duplicati-database-tool cleanup` reported the server database as orphaned, so `cleanup --force` deleted the live `Duplicati-server.sqlite`. It also deleted the copy of the server database that is made before a schema upgrade, and any `.sqlite` file from other applications in the data folder. Cleanup now only deletes orphaned local and sync databases, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Stopping a backup

Continuing the work from the previous canaries, "Stop now" no longer waits for a stuck source listing. A stop or abort pressed while the task was still being set up, which often happened on the first run after the server started, was dropped and is now kept, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Notifications

A backup that ended with a warning or error added a new notification without removing the one from its earlier run, so notifications could grow to thousands. Only the latest run's notification is now kept. "Dismiss all" now uses a single request instead of one per notification, and reading and dismissing a notification no longer loads all of them, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Storage provider fixes

- WebDAV listings on Linux and macOS failed when the folder name had an escaped character such as `#` or a space, a problem since 2.2.0.1, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Jottacloud downloads and listings could hang forever when the server stopped sending. They now observe `--read-write-timeout`, thanks @djdubd.
- `--s3-list-api-version` had no effect with the AWS client. The undocumented `--list-api-version` option still works but is now reported as deprecated, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Neon Object Storage is added to the S3 provider list, thanks @rishi-raj-jain.

# Other fixes

- Behind a reverse proxy that does not pass the Host header on, the browser rejected the refresh token cookie and the login looped. The cookie is now set for the host the browser asked for, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- If the server was restarted while the machine was suspended, it stayed paused after the restart, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- `AUTOUPDATER_Duplicati_SKIP_UPDATE` now stops all update checks, as the help text says, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The `Template` report output format now uses the bundled templates and fills in the values, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- `preload.json` is now read by more tools, and DatabaseTool, SourceTool and SecretTool have their own sections. DatabaseTool and SourceTool used to read the `serverutil` section, so settings meant for them there must be moved to `databasetool` or `sourcetool`, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Security hardening

- A multi-destination backup that fails no longer logs the full destination configuration, which could contain secrets.
- The recovery tool now rejects file names from the storage that would write outside the target folder.
- The Agent pre-shared key is now compared in constant time.
- StreamJsonRpc, MimeKit and System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs were updated to address published advisories, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

## Detailed list of changes

- Added support for Duplicati Storage as a secondary destination

name: v2.4.0.104_canary_2026-10-11
body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Hyper-V and MSSQL as source providers

Hyper-V virtual machines and MSSQL databases were previously added to a backup by replacing the `%HYPERV%` and `%MSSQL%` source paths with the real paths of the VM and database files. The backup then held those raw paths, and at restore time the user had to work out which files belong to which machine or database.

The two modules are now source providers that present the same files under a virtual folder per machine or database, with the machine or database name stored as metadata. The restore view can then group the files and show the names instead of GUIDs, and the UI source picker lists the same tree.

Building on this, a restore can now target the original location, where the destination is read from the metadata. A check before the restore starts reports files that are in use, such as a running virtual machine or an attached database. With the new `--register-restored-items` option, a restored Hyper-V machine is registered with Hyper-V after the restore. Both options are only available on Windows.

# Advanced options when restoring

A restore started from the UI can now be given advanced options that are not part of the backup configuration, so settings can be adjusted for a single restore without changing the backup.

# Links and junctions are restored correctly

Several problems with restoring symbolic links and directory junctions were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- A directory junction is now recorded as a junction and restored as one on Windows, instead of as a directory symbolic link. Backups made before this release have no kind recorded and restore as before.
- Restoring a symbolic link no longer removes a folder with files in it, or a file without `--overwrite`, that has taken the place of the link since the backup. The link is skipped with a warning instead.
- A link to a folder is now made only after the files below it are restored, which removes a race that caused "Could not find a part of the path" warnings and lost timestamps.
- Folders that a partial restore has to make for the files it restores are no longer reported as warnings.
- Restoring multiple paths with no common root on Windows no longer fails with "index out of bounds", and restoring from a UNC path to a local path works again.

# Windows snapshot cleanup

A snapshot that failed after its snapshot set was started left the set in progress. Every later snapshot then failed with `VSS_E_SNAPSHOT_SET_IN_PROGRESS` (0x80042316) until the process ended, and other VSS applications saw the same error. The snapshot manager is now disposed when setup fails, and a started set is aborted, thanks @stanleys12 and @JamBalaya56562.

# Stopping a backup on a stuck source

Continuing the work from the previous canary, "Stop now" now also returns when a source file open, size read or metadata read is stuck, such as on a network share that stopped answering, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# GnuPG on large volumes

GPG only finishes a volume after reading all of it, which took more than the fixed five seconds on large volumes and busy disks, so the backup failed with "program won't flush output" and could crash the process afterwards. The encryption now waits for GPG to finish without a time limit and reports a failed copy to the caller, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Storage provider fixes

- Azure Blob Storage uploads are now sent in blocks instead of a single request, so a volume that took longer than the network timeout to send no longer fails. The block size defaults to 10 MiB and can be lowered with `--azure-upload-block-size` for slow connections, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Google Cloud Storage uploads now include a CRC32 checksum, so a transfer error is less likely to leave a defective file in the bucket.
- Resumable uploads to Google services no longer fail when the server answers with a 308 status.
- Uploads to a Storj bucket with Object Lock no longer fail because of the default expiry time, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Parallel downloads from Jottacloud no longer end with "Stream position mismatch after download", thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A new `--enable-smb311` option connects to SMB servers that require SMB 3.1.1. It is off by default as the library marks it experimental, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- HashiCorp Vault secrets that arrive as JSON elements are now read, which fixes "The following keys were not found", thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Microsoft 365 enumeration

Enumerating mailboxes no longer requests the message body, which made listings large and slow. Emails are enumerated through the delta endpoint, which has stable pagination and avoids the repeated enumeration that caused long delays and duplicate-item warnings. Locked sites are skipped, OneNote and ToDo access is only warned about once, inherited permissions are no longer requested for items without explicit permissions, transient network errors are retried, and heavy throttling is handled with longer waits. A new `--office365-exclude-system-libraries` option excludes system libraries in sites and groups.

# Remote access on NAS devices

On Synology and QNAP, Duplicati authentication is tied to the system login, so the relayed requests used by the console were rejected because Duplicati itself is not a NAS user. A local forwarding key, generated at startup, now lets Duplicati authenticate its own requests.

# Backups from remote sources

Backups that read from a remote source such as SMB or S3 now return rooted paths in the listing, store metadata in the virtual root so the UI knows the data cannot be restored directly to the source, and work with USN change journals active.

# Sync operation logs and database update

Sync operations now write their results into the sync database, so the outcome of each run is shown in the job log, as it is for backups. The log entries are purged by the `--log-retention` option.

This requires an update of the sync database schema to version 1, which adds the log table. The update is applied automatically on first use, and after it the sync database can no longer be opened by earlier versions of Duplicati. If you need to downgrade, the bundled database tool (`duplicati-database-tool`) can downgrade the sync database back to version 0. Downgrading removes the stored sync logs, but otherwise causes no data loss. Backup databases are not affected.

## Detailed list of changes

- Changed Hyper-V and MSSQL to be source providers with a virtual folder per machine or database, thanks @JamBalaya56562
- Added support for restoring Hyper-V and MSSQL items to their original location
- Added the `--register-restored-items` option to register a restored Hyper-V machine

body:
# About this release

This release patches version 2.4.0.0 with fixes for a number of issues that were discovered after the release.
The main focus of this release is stability, with many fixes to restore, abort handling and the new sync mode, along with security hardening of the server and remote control.

## Usability fixes

The search feature would allow you to select files, but would send incorrect paths to the restore flow.
On Windows, this would result in no files selected in the search view being restored.

## Security and Privacy

The login setup has been hardened against weak passwords, the remote control requests have been locked down and require per-message keys.
The remote control connection now works on NAS devices that use integrated authentication (Synology DSM).
Path redaction in logs and reports has been improved, and secrets in lists now have an additional layer of protection.

A new reduced reporting mode (`--reduced-reporting`) limits reports leaving the machine to log message ids, counters and dates, without message text, error messages or file names. The HTTP status report has a matching `--http-report-status-reduced-reporting` option. The setting can also be enforced from the console for users requiring it.

## Restore and Abort Fixes

A restore now carries on with the next file when a single file fails, instead of stopping the whole restore. Several issues that could cause a restore to hang have been fixed, including releasing blocks for skipped files, releasing all restore processes when a volume cannot be produced, and releasing the restore stages on every exit path. A missing destination folder is now reported before the restore starts.

Aborting a backup or other operation no longer waits for a stuck source file read, a stuck backend call, or a block processor that has stopped. Aborting a repair while it reads the local database no longer discards the database.

## Sync Mode Fixes

The sync mode introduced in 2.4.0.0 has received a number of fixes: folder sync on some destinations, zero-byte uploads to Google Drive and Google Cloud, case-insensitive remotes, duplicate remote listings, sync metadata and last-run handling, and lower memory use by not storing remote operations in memory. The synchronization tool now passes the correct arguments to its backends, ignores folder entries in listings, renames through the backend, and counts failed deletes and renames in its return code.

## Stability and Performance

The wasted space calculation used for compacting has been improved, deleting filesets uses less memory, and SQLite memory usage has been further reduced.
Database connections are now closed when opening or setting up a local database fails, and the server now takes the database lock in a few paths that previously skipped it.
Resuming after sleep no longer waits for the suspend handling to finish, and Windows is allowed to sleep again when an operation ends.
Tasks and HTTP status reports now report errors from operations that finished without throwing.

## Backend and Provider Fixes

- Google Drive: keep every copy of a duplicated name, and report no quota for shared drives instead of the user's own quota.
- Google Workspace: handle inactive accounts, emit a root folder, and fix the restore scope.
- MS365: fix restore of large emails.
- Drime: fix incomplete listings beyond the pagination limit.
- S3: add RelAix to the list of providers.
- SMB: improved error detection.
- Duplicati backend: show error messages from the console.
- An unknown destination quota is no longer treated as a full destination, and the manual quota is kept when the backend quota is disabled.

## Windows Installer and Shell Integration

The MSI now remembers the install location on upgrade, and the path browse button has been fixed.
The Windows shell overlay has been fixed. It requires the folder status service, which is disabled by default and can only be enabled from the commandline with `--webservice-enable-folder-status-service=true`.

## Other Changes

The command line tools have a number of fixes to listing and searching, such as listing the latest version when none is given, searching sub-folders, looking up file versions by full path, and handling folders given without a trailing separator. Purge and set-locks now stop when the given version or time matches no fileset, and a queued command keeps the versions it named when it was sent.
The old UI has fixes for editing local folder and S3 destinations, restore version grouping and selecting a restore root.
This release also adds an option to prevent the server from creating a new database (`--webservice-dont-autocreate-database`), support for runner identity and license usage collection, and fixes for packaging `libc_wrapper.so` and for running when the account has no home folder.

name: v2.4.0.103_canary_2026-10-02
body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Reduced reporting mode

A new reduced reporting mode limits everything that is sent outside the machine to log message ids, counters, dates and stack traces. No message text, error message or file name is transmitted, and the bug report feature is disabled. The mode is enabled with `--reduced-reporting`, overrides the regular path redaction, also applies to the data handed to run-scripts, and cannot be undone by a backup configuration. Local log data is still available in full.

# Recreate with defective filelists

A failed transfer can leave a partially written filelist on the remote storage. The backup would then fail because of the unknown file, and recreating the database failed because the partial file could not be read. The database recreate now probes the filelists and continues without the defective ones. The next backup will then ask for a `repair`, which removes the offending files.

# Restore fixes

A number of problems in the restore flow were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- A file that cannot be created or written no longer stops the restore of the files after it.
- A restore that finishes with errors is now reported as failed in the UI and in the HTTP status report, instead of showing as successful.
- Skipped files, including files where a copy already exists, no longer cause `BlockCountError` and `VolumeCountError` messages.
- A missing destination folder is reported before the restore starts instead of after the full retry delay.
- More cases where a failing restore stage could leave the restore waiting forever are now released.
- The restore tree no longer hides a source whose path extends the name of another source file, and a backup with multiple drives no longer takes 30 seconds per drive to list.

# Stopping a backup no longer hangs (or at least less often)

Using "Stop now" could leave the backup waiting forever if a source file read was stuck, such as on a network share that stopped answering, or if a block processor was stopped while holding a block. Both cases now return as cancelled, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Windows sleep, resume and port fixes

Three Windows related problems were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- With `--allow-sleep` disabled, Windows was kept awake after the operation had finished. The sleep prevention is now withdrawn when the operation ends.
- If the machine was suspended before the pause was fully handled, the server could stay paused after waking up.
- The server now tries the next port when Windows refuses the port, such as when port 8200 is in a range reserved for Hyper-V, WSL or Docker.

# MSI installer remembers the install location

A custom install location chosen in the MSI installer is now remembered for later upgrades. Older packages did not record the location, so this takes effect from the next upgrade. The location can also be set with `msiexec /i package.msi INSTALLLOCATION=C:\OtherLocation`, which works for silent installs. The browse button for picking the path was also fixed.

# Queued commands keep their version

A command sent from the command line page in the UI waits in the task queue. If a backup ran before the command, the `--version` numbers had shifted, so a delete could remove the wrong version. The versions are now resolved when the command is sent, and the command is not run if a named version no longer exists, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Synchronization improvements

Sync jobs now keep their own metadata and only update it when the operation succeeds, instead of writing the last backup values even on failures. The remote operation log is no longer kept in memory during a sync, and uploading a zero-byte file to Google Cloud Storage or Google Drive no longer fails with a 400 error.

This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# New restore-test command

A new `restore-test` command restores a sample of files from a backup into a temporary folder and verifies them. The sample size, download budget, runtime and version can be controlled with the `--restore-test-*` options. For backups, the option `--perform-restore-test-after` runs the restore test automatically after a given amount of time.

# Choosing a VSS provider

Windows snapshots can now use a specific VSS provider with `--vss-provider-id=<guid>`. The snapshot setup also detects a provider that does not expose mapped paths and cannot be used. If no provider is selected, it falls back to the Microsoft Software Shadow Copy provider.

# Lower memory usage when deleting versions

Deleting, compacting, purging and repairing forced SQLite to build a large in-memory table holding all fileset entries being removed. The filesets are now removed one at a time, which bounds memory use to a single version. On a synthetic database with 100 versions and 300k files this was 16-20% faster with an 80% reduction in memory. The wasted space calculation was also rewritten and is roughly 9x faster on large databases.

# Synchronization tool fixes

A number of problems in the remote synchronization tool were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- The backend managers received the wrong arguments, so a missing source folder was created and the empty listing deleted every file in the destination.
- Folder entries reported by the destination are now ignored instead of failing the run.
- Renames now use the backend's own rename and content verification compares through temporary files, reducing peak memory from gigabytes to under 100 MB for large volumes.
- Failed deletes and renames are now counted in the return code instead of reporting success.
- A destination with mode interval or counting but no interval or count was only synchronized once. It now runs inline with a warning.
- The `--case-insensitive-remote` option is now honoured, so a case-only rename no longer loses the file on case-insensitive destinations.
- The primary sync database is now closed when the run ends, and the `--sync-remote-state` warning names values the option accepts.

Additionally, the tool no longer fails to copy folders on backends that report paths with a trailing separator.

# Restore and backup no longer hang on failures

A restore that hit a volume it could not download, decrypt or decompress could wait forever instead of failing. All restore stages are now released when a volume cannot be produced. Similarly, stopping a backup while a backend call was stuck in a transfer that did not observe cancellation left the operation waiting; the backend manager now abandons the call and the operation returns as cancelled, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Path redaction in reports

Additional checks prevent file paths from being included in logs and reports sent outside the system. The option `--allow-paths-in-log-messages` disables the redaction for environments where paths can be reported safely.

# Selecting which operations send reports

The mail, HTTP, XMPP and Telegram reporting modules have a new option, such as `--send-mail-operations`, that selects which operations emit a report. The default is to report backups only, as before.

# Command-line listing fixes

Several listing commands did not behave as documented, thanks @JamBalaya56562:

- `list-folder-contents` now accepts a folder without a trailing separator and picks the latest version when no time or version is given.
- `search` now searches sub-folders of the given folder.

This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Fixed Linux data folder for services without a home folder

When running as a Linux service under an account with no home folder, the data folder was stored as the relative path `var/lib/Duplicati` instead of `/var/lib/Duplicati`. Relative paths are now resolved correctly, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Fixed sync failing on backends that cannot report quota

A backend that cannot report free space returns a negative value. The synchronization tool compared this against the required size and incorrectly concluded the destination was full, stopping the sync. The quota check now only runs when the destination actually reported a free space, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Fixed sync crash on duplicate remote file names

A remote listing that reported the same name twice made the synchronization tool fail with an unhelpful `ArgumentException`. It now reports which side has the duplicates and what to do about it, matching the message the backup path already produced, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Fixed source lost inside an excluded folder

A source folder nested inside another source, with a folder on the path between them excluded, was silently dropped from the backup. The nested source was converted to an include filter, but the containing source's enumeration never descended into the excluded folder, so the filter was never reached. Such sources are now kept as sources instead of being converted to filters, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Faster consistency checks

The database consistency check queries were rewritten to avoid SQLite building automatic indexes. Depending on database size and shape, the checks are now 25-40% faster, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# New option to prevent automatic database creation

The new `--webservice-dont-autocreate-database` option prevents the server from creating an empty database on startup. Useful when the database already exists and you want the server to fail rather than start with an empty configuration due to a misconfigured data folder.

# Fixed MS365 large email restore

Restoring large emails to an MS365 tenant previously failed because the restore path attempted to set read-only or non-nullable properties on the email creation request. Only writable properties are now sent, and null values are omitted.

# Fixed full-disk backup on Linux and macOS

The native wrapper libraries (`libc_wrapper.so`, `libSystem_wrapper.dylib`) were placed in a `runtimes` subfolder by the build but the P/Invoke loader only looked in the application folder, causing full-disk backup to fail on packaged installs. A resolver now probes both locations.

body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# New Native VSS snapshot provider

This release introduces a new native VSS snapshot provider on Windows that replaces the previous providers. Hyper-V and MSSQL enumeration work with the native provider which is now default.

The new native VSS snapshot provider does not require VCRedist to be installed and works on x86, x64, and Arm64 systems.
The existing AlphaVSS and Vanara-based VSS snapshot providers can still be selected (but not on Arm64).
They will be removed in a future version as AlphaVSS is no longer maintained and the new native library has fewer dependencies than Vanara.

# New WMI VSS snapshot provider

The previously supported WMIC provider has been removed as Windows updates will remove the executable it relies on.
Instead a new WMI snapshot provider is added which works similar to WMIC.

The WMI (and WMIC) provider gives a more light-weight VSS functionality, where it does not flush the writers (MSSQL, HyperV, etc) but just ensures a crash-consistent disk snapshot.

If you rely on systems that integrate with VSS, use the Native provider, if you just want to back up locked files, use the WMI provider.

# Full-disk backup and VSS snapshots

With this release VSS is now also used for full-disk backups. This is fully transparent and works such that an active snapshot is detected and the full-disk reader will use the snapshot to access the disk contents.

# Recovering from an interrupted first backup

Interrupting a first backup previously left the destination in an unrecoverable state: blocks and index files were uploaded, but no filelist was written, so neither backup nor repair could proceed. The recreate logic can now reconstruct a database from the index files alone, so an interrupted first backup can be resumed instead of requiring the destination to be discarded, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Repair no longer removes metadata

The repair handler previously attempted to fix defective metadata with various reassignment strategies that could silently remove metadata. It now reports the problem and asks the user to run `list-broken-files` and `purge-broken-files`, which rewire the metadata while keeping the file content. Detection of zero-length and otherwise defective blocksets has also been improved.

# Azure Blob Storage path support

The Azure Blob Storage backend previously ignored the path part of the destination URL and always stored data in the root of the container. The path is now treated as a prefix, so backups can be placed in a subfolder of a container. If you previously used a path in an Azure Blob Storage destination URL, the data was stored in the root; after upgrading, new backups will use the path as a prefix and will not see the previously uploaded files.

# Prevent empty machine ID

A startup sequence issue could cause a clean install to report and connect to the console without a machine ID, which could cause various unwanted behaviors.

# Linux sleep prevention

Duplicati can now prevent the system from sleeping during backup operations on Linux, similar to the existing support on Windows and macOS.

# AppImage `.zsync` support

This release now has the `.zsync` file and relevant metadata such that future updates can be done efficiently and automatically by AppImage managers that support it.

# `--synchronous-upload` deprecated

The `--synchronous-upload` option no longer has any effect and is now marked as deprecated. Existing configurations that set it will continue to load, but a warning is now logged. Use `--asynchronous-upload-limit` instead.

# Default exclude volume information

The `System Volume Information` folder is now automatically excluded from backups as it cannot be reliably read and cannot be used in a restore process.

# Performance and stability updates

Several performance fixes are applied to the local database queries, affecting most operations, mostly by @JamBalaya56562.
Many edge cases around unexpected server responses and url encoding issues have also been adressed, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

name: v2.4.0.0_stable_2026-09-03
body:
This release is a stable release that supersedes the 2.3.0.4 stable release. It contains all changes from the 2.3.1.0 and 2.3.1.1 beta releases.

# Breaking change: Locked-down data folder permissions

This release hardens security around the data folder and is a **breaking change** for some setups.

_For most users, this should not be a problem as the folders should already have the correct permissions._

Duplicati now **requires** that the data folder has the exact expected permissions, or it will refuse to use it. Previously, Duplicati would silently lock down the folder if it was not already locked.

To opt out of the permission check, you need to either pass `--allow-insecure-datafolder`, set the environment variable `DUPLICATI__ALLOW_INSECURE_DATAFOLDER=true`, or place a file named `insecure-permissions.txt` in the installation folder.

Note that the previous method of placing `insecure-permissions.txt` in the data folder is no longer supported.

This change also applies to `preload.json`, such that it will only be loaded if the folder is trusted, or one of the opt-out methods are activated. Additionally, the previous trusted paths `/usr/local/share/Duplicati/preload.json` and `C:\ProgramData\Duplicati\preload.json` are no longer supported as they cannot be guaranteed to be locked down.

A `preload.json` inside the data folder is still supported, provided the folder passes the permission check.

The `ConfigureTool` has a new `secure-datafolder` command that can be used to force the correct permissions on the data folder.

For most users this should not cause any problems, as Duplicati has been locking down the folder already, but if you rely on lax folder permissions the setup needs to change. Some Docker setups may not be able to set the permissions and will need to apply `DUPLICATI__ALLOW_INSECURE_DATAFOLDER=true` in the image to run without the protections.

# Sync copy mode

This release adds an often requested feature that enables simple copying of files from source to destination.
Where the regular backups are deduplicated, compressed, encrypted and versioned, the new sync mode will instead simply copy from source to destination.

The copy is currently a one-way sync, where the source is replicated on the destination. Files can be deleted on the destination during sync (use `--sync-then-delete`), but destination folders will not be deleted.

The option `--sync-remote-state` is by default set to `UseRemoteState` which will list the destination and figure out what to upload. The setting `UseLocalState` uses a local database, similar to how backups work, to keep track of known remote files, and reduce the amount of remote listings done. Finally, the `BlindlyUpload` setting will just copy everything as-is to the remote.

The sync jobs support remote sources, snapshots, and multiple destinations. If snapshots are enabled, the copy is done from the snapshot, ensuring reliable reads.

Configuration of such a sync job is done the same way as with backup, but using a toggle option in the first step of the UI. Note that backup and sync jobs are not compatible as they use very different storage logic, so it is not possible to change the job mode after creating a job.

CLI mode also supports sync.

# Improved Windows installer

This change brings a major update to the Windows installers, which now integrates the ability to run as a service, as well as generate and use TLS (https). The service feature has been present for a while in the `WindowsService.exe` tool and the TLS certificates were added as part of the `Duplicati.CommandLine.ConfigureTool.exe`. With this update these things are now integrated into the installer, and exposed as simple checkboxes to toggle the features. Installing the service from a regular user account, will also auto-generate a secure password and configure the TrayIcon to connect to the service (only for the current user).

If you have installed the service manually, do not activate the new checkbox as it only works if there is no pre-existing service. The installer-driven service does not support commandline arguments directly, but instead prefers `preload.json` files to configure it. The MSI supports the property `INSTALL_PRELOAD=true` which will cause it to pick up a `preload.json` file from the same folder the MSI is located in.

The Windows service is now also configured as delay-start service to avoid startup issues on boot.

# Live reporting module

This release adds a new live-reporting module that sends the current progress of backups to a user-specified URL. The intention is that this can be used for dashboards that want to show the current progress for backups. By default, the module is not configured and has no impact.

The module supports multiple activity targets and includes metadata in the activity report, as well as a console-provided activity URL.

# PAR2 parity / error-correction for remote volumes

This release adds a pluggable parity module that produces error-correction data for remote data volumes, so they can be repaired after bit-rot or corruption on the backend, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

To enable this, ensure that `par2` is installed on the machine and set `--parity-module=par2`. Setting this will cause additional `.par2` files to be uploaded.

# Store configuration with backup

This release revives the `store-task-config` option and makes it enabled by default for encrypted backups. The backup configuration is stored with the backup data, making it easier to restore a configuration later.

For unencrypted backups, no secrets are stored by default. The behavior can be customized with options to store none, self, or all configurations, with or without secrets. The UI has been updated to allow restoring from the destination config. If multiple configurations are found, the user can select one or more backup configurations to restore.

# MS365 subsites and shared mailboxes

This release improves the Microsoft 365 backup support with two additions.
Support for backing up SharePoint subsites has been added, making it possible to include sub-sites beneath a site collection in a backup.

The handling of shared mailboxes has also been improved, with better detection and enumeration of shared mailboxes within a tenant.

The license counting has been simplified. A Duplicati license is now required if an MS365 license is assigned, without needing per-user lookups. The same logic applies to both users and sites, and personal sites of users without a license are not counted. Filtering based on classification is still supported.

# Full disk backup support (Windows, Linux, MacOS)

This release extends the full disk backup feature to support Linux and MacOS, in addition to Windows.

The Linux support allows backup and restore of entire disks on Linux, including partition tables. The MacOS support adds basic backup and restore of entire disks, including partition tables.

Partition-level backup and restore is now supported, making it possible to select individual partitions as backup sources, or restore a single partition from a full disk backup to a different partition.

Like the Office 365 / Google Workspace backup features, this is a proprietary module (source available).

Full disk backup requires administrative privileges to access the disk directly.
Full disk restore requires administrative privileges and requires that the disk is unmounted and not write-protected.

# Desktop notifications on all platforms

Desktop notifications are now supported on all platforms. Windows toast notifications have been implemented with click-to-open support, and native notification support has been added for macOS and Linux (via DBus), thanks @JamBalaya56562 for the Windows implementation.

# Restore reliability improvements

Several issues with the restore process have been fixed. Restores now properly respond to stop/abort requests, file reads and writes can be interrupted, and a critical bug with wrong seek offsets for partial blocks has been fixed, which could cause restores to fail, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

An index has been added on the restore file table join columns for better restore performance, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

# Misconfigured filter detection

A new warning system detects when filters are configured to unconditionally exclude everything. A post-backup check also warns if no files were examined during backup, which helps catch misconfigurations that would otherwise silently produce empty backups.

# New backends

Added support for Drime Cloud as a new storage backend.

Added a new backend for the Spanish provider Movistar, thanks @redmars27. The backend is marked as "untested" as it can only be used (and tested) by Movistar customers.

# Deprecated backends

The previous "SharePoint" and "OneDrive for Business" backends have been marked as deprecated, as Microsoft shut down the API they were calling. The migration step is to use the "SharePoint v2" backend (renamed to just "SharePoint" in this version) which uses the Microsoft Graph API.

# Duplicati Storage

This release includes Duplicati Storage which is integrated with the Duplicati console. Once a machine is connected to the console it can use the account's storage allocations with zero configuration required.

# SharpAESCrypt v3

Updated the SharpAESCrypt encryption library to support "AES Crypt Stream Format v3", which has a number of improvements over the v2 format.
For this release, the default written format remains v2, but we encourage you to set the environment variable `DUPLICATI__AES_VERSION=3` to test the new format.
**Note:** if you set this version to 3, the new remote volumes cannot be read by Duplicati versions older than 2.3.0.101.

# Support for MacOS ACLs

This release adds support for reading MacOS attributes and ACL strings during backup, and restoring them when permission restores are selected.

# Support for Windows Alternate Data Streams

This release implements support for reading and writing alternate data streams (ADS) on Windows. This feature is disabled by default and can be enabled with the advanced option `--enable-ads-backup`. If ADS content is found in the source, this is restored by default but can be disabled with `--disable-ads-restore`.

# Fixed MSSQL backups

Since 2.1 the MSSQL backups would produce errors if attempting to back up an MSSQL server that was running as the default instance, but would work with a named instance. This release fixes the issue and now handles both default- and named instances.

# Improved missing source handling

The default behavior when sources are missing has changed. Previously, a missing source would abort the backup. Now, a missing source will only trigger a warning unless the option `--abort-if-source-missing` is set. The option `--allow-missing-source` can still be used to suppress warnings entirely. If no sources are found at all, the backup will still abort.

# Relative database paths

Database paths are now stored relative to the data folder by default. This makes it simpler to move the data folder as the paths are not stored in full. Existing backups retain their full paths, but manually updating a database path will make it relative if it is within the data folder.

# Improved TLS certificate validation

The TLS certificate validation has been improved, and Duplicati now falls back to using the OS-default certificate validator. This should resolve issues with custom certificate chains and improve compatibility with various TLS setups.

# Improved source tree and filter accuracy

The source tree now shows the content of remote sources, including Microsoft 365 tenants, Google Workspace subscriptions and full-disk content. Filter evaluation is performed server-side for non-trivial filters, ensuring the same code is used for display and actual backup operations.

Helper entries like "My Documents" are now shown in all picker situations and resolve to the full path. The destination configuration supports browsing the remote file system.

# New welcome page and start

The UI will now show a welcome page showing how to connect to the console with an option to continue without.
This can be suppressed with the option `--webservice-suppress-welcome-page=true` or environment variable `DUPLICATI__WEBSERVICE_SUPPRESS_WELCOME_PAGE=true`.

If the connection is made from the TrayIcon, the initial dialog asking to set a password is no longer shown, as the intention is to use the TrayIcon to connect.
It is still possible to change the password from the Settings page if needed.

# Other notable changes

- **AutoTune tool**: A new `Duplicati.CommandLine.AutoTuneTool` / `duplicati-autotune` tool to help evaluate and optimize performance-related settings.
- **Read-only backend testing**: Backends now support read-only context-aware testing, safe for testing restore destinations without risking unintended changes.
- **Remote synchronization improvements**: Integrated remote synchronization (3-2-1 backups) into the Main library with quota checks and improved error handling.
- **Multi-version restore**: New `--restore-all-files` option to restore files matching a filter from multiple versions.
- **Performance improvements**: ArrayPool-based allocations reduce memory pressure during backups. Faster delete queries for large backups.
- **Post-backup scripts**: The RunScript module now supports running scripts when a backup has finished, but before checks and compaction.
- **Database tool commands**: Added `verify` and `cleanup` commands to the database tool. Added `wipe-encryption` command for recovering encrypted databases.
- **Slow query monitor**: Added tracking of long-running database queries to help diagnose performance issues.
- **Crash dialog**: Added a crash dialog window that appears when the application encounters an unhandled exception.
- **Updated LibSecret support** for KDE Plasma 5+6, fixing issues with the default collection.
- **More robust server connection**: The remote server connection has been hardened with a watchdog that restarts unresponsive connections.
- **Auto-configure database metadata**: The `--store-metadata-content-in-database` option is automatically applied when needed by the source provider.
- **MS365/Google permission testing**: Added ability to verify that granted permissions match what is required for backup or restore.

# Thanks to contributors

This release is a collaboration effort from the Duplicati community. Thanks to the many contributors who report issues, test new releases, request features, write documentation, maintain translations, and contribute to the codebase.

# 2026-08-26 - 2.3.1.1_beta_2026-08-26

This release is a Beta release intended to be used for testing to identify any issues before releasing the next stable version.

# Partition level full disk backup and restore

The full disk backup feature now supports selecting individual partitions as backup sources, in addition to entire disks. This makes it more intuitive to back up a specific partition without filtering.

Restore now also supports partition-to-partition restores, so it is possible to restore a single partition from a full disk backup, or restore a partition backup to a different partition.

Desktop notifications are now supported on all platforms. Windows toast notifications have been implemented (with click-to-open support), and native notification support has been added for macOS and Linux (via DBus), thanks @JamBalaya56562.

A new warning system detects when filters are configured to unconditionally exclude everything. A post-backup check also warns if no files were examined during backup, which helps catch misconfigurations that would otherwise silently produce empty backups.

The remote server connection has been hardened against network events that could cause it to drop. A watchdog monitors the connection and restarts it if it has been unresponsive for an extended period.

The database query for deleting old backup versions has been optimized, significantly speeding up the delete operation for large backups.

name: v2.3.0.110_canary_2026-08-25
body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Database update to version 20

This release updates the local database schema to version 20. The update adds a label column to the fileset table and is applied automatically on first use. After the update, the database can no longer be opened by earlier versions of Duplicati. If you need to downgrade, the bundled database tool (`duplicati-database-tool`) can downgrade the database back to version 19; downgrading removes the labels, but otherwise causes no data loss.

# Labels on backup versions

Backup versions can now carry an optional text label. Labels have no functional purpose, but they help mark and distinguish versions, for example when backups are hand-curated instead of running on a schedule. The CLI and UI supports setting and showing labels.

# Partition-level backup and restore

It is now possible to select a single disk partition as the backup source, instead of selecting the full disk and filtering the unwanted partitions. Restores are likewise more flexible: in addition to disk-to-disk restores, a single partition can now be restored into a partition on another disk, creating the partition as needed.

This also fixes a bug where a failing priority file would leave the restore stuck until it was cancelled, and a number of issues with enumerating and filtering disks and partitions, in particular on Windows.

# Automatic metadata storage for sources that need it

Backups using a source provider that relies on database metadata, such as the disk image provider, previously required the user to set `--store-metadata-content-in-database=true` manually. The setting is now applied automatically when the source needs it, and can still be overridden by setting the option explicitly.

# QNAP packages

This release adds native QNAP package support. Similar to the Synology package, it integrates with the QNAP OS, uses the built-in authentication, and only allows access for administrators.

# Stricter Google Cloud Storage credentials

Google Cloud Storage credentials are now read as service account credentials, which is what the options are documented to take. Other credential types, such as stored user credentials or external account configurations, are now refused. If you authenticate to Google Cloud Storage, or the Google Cloud secret provider, with anything other than a service account key, you need to switch to a service account key.

## Detailed list of changes

- Updated all localizations, thanks to all translators
- Added labels to backup versions, with CLI, API, and UI support
- Added partition-level backup and partition-to-partition restore
- Fixed disk image provider not initializing when listing drives, and improved disk enumeration and filter handling on Windows
- Automatically enabled `--store-metadata-content-in-database` when the source provider requires it
- Added native QNAP package support
- Added a watchdog that restarts a stale remote management connection, and fixed issues that could drop the connection

- Fixed WebDAV destinations with a `+` in the path reporting uploaded files as missing, thanks @JamBalaya56562
- Fixed Windows `file://` target URLs with a query string being misparsed
- Stopped reporting quota errors on read-only operations such as restore, thanks @JamBalaya56562
- Fixed stale SQLite query statistics causing extremely slow fileset and consistency queries on growing databases, thanks @JamBalaya56562
- Sped up cleanup after deleting a backup version by avoiding a full table scan
- Fixed a similarly named file and folder in the source causing the folder to be omitted, and allowed explicitly including a file inside an excluded folder
- Fixed backend statistics reporting a bogus zero timestamp in the operation log, thanks @JamBalaya56562
- Fixed Linux desktop notifications using an unsupported signal API, thanks @JamBalaya56562
- Fixed a restore with failing priority files getting stuck instead of failing
- Aligned SharpAESCrypt, AWSSDK.Core, Azure.Core, and Microsoft.Extensions package versions across the solution, thanks @JamBalaya56562

## Updates to ngclient

name: v2.3.0.109_canary_2026-08-14
body:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.

# Native desktop notifications

This release adds native desktop notifications on all supported desktop platforms. Backup results and other tray-icon notifications are now shown as real operating-system notifications instead of only appearing inside the UI.

On Windows, notifications are shown as Windows toast notifications with click-to-open support, thanks @JamBalaya56562. On macOS, notifications are shown via the native notification center. On Linux, notifications are sent over DBus and integrate with the desktop environment's notification daemon.

# Native environment variable syntax on Linux and macOS

Paths and filters now support the native `$VAR` and `${VAR}` environment variable syntax on Linux and macOS, most notably `$HOME`, thanks @JamBalaya56562. Previously only the Windows-style `%VAR%` syntax was expanded, so the native forms were silently left unexpanded on non-Windows systems.

The expansion is additive: `%VAR%` keeps working everywhere, and an undefined variable is left as-is. If you previously worked around this with literal `$` characters in paths or filters, those entries will now be expanded.

# Restore improvements and fixes

Several restore issues have been fixed in this release, thanks @JamBalaya56562. Restore now honors stop requests promptly: an abort interrupts in-progress file reads and writes, where it previously could keep running for minutes after the request. An aborted restore no longer reports errors, blames the backup, or leaks temporary files, and files that a shutdown interrupted are no longer listed as broken. A requested shutdown is in general no longer reported as a failure. Two bugs that could corrupt restored data were fixed: a wrong seek offset when copying verified local blocks, and an incorrect buffer copy when merging a hash fragment. Restore now also preserves the selected folder and applies configured default options (such as `--restore-permissions`) when the restore request does not explicitly specify them. On the legacy restore engine, restoring a directory symlink no longer creates a real folder in its place.

# Stricter validation of settings

This release adds validation in places that previously failed silently, which may surface new warnings or errors after upgrading:

- Misconfigured filters are now detected and reported with a warning, instead of silently matching nothing.
- An unusable update check interval is now rejected instead of being ignored.
- An invalid webservice timezone now fails instead of being silently reset.
